This study investigates the relationship between digital reporting systems and organisational accountability in public universities. The research adopts a mixed-methods design, combining a survey of one hundred and twenty administrative staff with twelve semi-structured interviews. Furthermore, the analysis examines how reporting requirements influence day-to-day record keeping in three faculties. The findings indicate that staff perceive the system as useful, although the additional documentation increases their workload during the registration period. Moreover, the study finds that accountability practices vary across departments, particularly where external audits are frequent. These variations are not fully explained by the technology itself. The paper concludes that reporting systems should be studied alongside the institutional routines they replace, rather than as standalone tools.
